elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 6.1 now reads "The Company may participate in any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products, and HDI shall have no exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand." The prohibition ("shall not participate in any project similar to the Site ... including ... Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar") is gone, and the Vendor exclusive over Customer's own "Deerskin" brand — a field-of-use restriction on Customer's use and licensing of its own brand — is expressly negated. No residual restriction on Customer's businesses or products remains in the rendered text; Section 6.2 is a Customer right, and Section 4.1 is unaffected.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the operative text no longer imposes any restriction on Customer, so there is no restriction whose scope could exceed a single named competing product. The prior open-ended "products substantially similar" / "companies similar to" scope has been struck.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the words "during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate ..." have been replaced by a permission, so no restriction runs during or after the term.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with no restriction remaining, the indefinite duration risk created by the annual auto-renewal in Section 4.1 no longer attaches to any covenant binding Customer.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied and affirmatively covered: Section 6.1 as rendered permits Customer to "participate in any project on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar," so internal development is unimpeded.
Vacuously satisfied: no covenant remains that could be triggered by an acquisition or an acquired business's competing products.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment — the prohibition and the HDI brand exclusive are both eliminated in the rendered Section 6.1.
The fallback elements are conditional on a surviving restriction; since no restriction remains, each is satisfied by non-application, so the redline is position-complete at both levels.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to Section 6.1, the clause targeted by the rule. Negating HDI's exclusive right over the "Deerskin" brand is required, not an extra, because a no-field-of-use result is incomplete while a Vendor exclusive prevents Customer from using or licensing its own brand. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or unrelated boilerplate was added.

Dropping the lead-in "Except as provided in Section 6.2" does not leave a dangling cross-reference: Section 6.2 is drafted as a standalone Customer retention of rights ("The Company retains the right to establish a web site ...") and survives intact rather than as an exception to a now-deleted prohibition.

Intent is preserved: Section 4.1 term/auto-renewal, the Section 6.2 closeout carve-out and the Vendor-side restriction in Section 6.3 (favourable to Customer) are untouched, and the new sentence negates only exclusivity — any non-exclusive HDI brand use needed to build and host the Site elsewhere in the Agreement is not contradicted.

Correctly not double-flagged: the Section 9(b) Globix-termination proviso is a sourcing/hosting condition, not a restriction on the businesses Customer may operate or the products it may buy or build, so it belongs outside this rule.

Drafting nit only (not a defect): the permission is phrased more broadly than the original prohibition ("any project" rather than "any project similar to the Site"). It operates solely within the subject matter of the deleted covenant, so it does not add a requirement outside the checklist, but the tighter formulation "may participate in any project, including any project similar to the Site," would track the struck language more closely if HDI pushes back.

Claimed finding status "deviation" is correct: the original Section 6.1 failed the fallback on scope (open-ended "products substantially similar" and "companies similar to"), duration (indefinite via annual auto-renewal, no 12-month cap), and the absence of internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
